public.scenario: Synthetic contrastive retry semantics, set A
public.task: For each mutating operation, decide whether a stable exact request key has an explicit, durable duplicate-suppression guarantee, or only supports tracing or an unsupported best-effort claim. Every operation is synthetic.

operations.description: Creates a warehouse slot hold with a request-key header. The key is stored durably for event correlation. Replaying that identical key, even after a dropped response, creates an additional hold; no uniqueness check runs.

Creates a warehouse slot hold with a request-key header. The key is stored durably. Replaying that identical key, even after a dropped response, returns the existing hold and never makes another hold.

Captures freight settlement with a stable transaction reference. A duplicate replay with the same reference is suppressed at commit by a uniqueness constraint; callers receive the previously committed settlement.

Captures freight settlement with a stable transaction reference. A duplicate replay with the same reference is recorded for reconciliation but is not suppressed at commit; a second settlement may be charged.
Assignments are accepted with dispatch_token. It is a searchable event field, not an enforced unique key: if the same token is retried, the service may create a second dispatch and additional fee.
Assignments are accepted with dispatch_token. It is an enforced unique key: if the same token is retried, the service returns the existing assignment without any second dispatch or additional fee.
Read-only status inspection, which may lag after a write. Does not itself create an external business effect.
